Galician

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

From a derivative of Latin medius.[1]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • meolo, molo

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈmolo̝/

Noun

[edit]

molo m (plural molos)

  1. central piece of the Galician cart wheel, which is united on its extremes with the cambas, or curved pieces of the wheel's felly, and has in its center the wheel's nave
    Synonyms: mil, mión, miúl

Etymology 2

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • miolo

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈmolo̝/

Noun

[edit]

molo m (plural molos)

  1. alternative form of miolo

References

[edit]
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, editor (2006–2013), “molo”, in Dicionario de Dicionarios da lingua galega [Dictionary of Dictionaries of the Galician language] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, Ernesto Xosé González Seoane, María Álvarez de la Granja, editors (2003–2018), “molo”, in Tesouro informatizado da lingua galega (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Rosario Álvarez Blanco, editor (2014–2024), “molo”, in Tesouro do léxico patrimonial galego e portugués (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega, →ISSN
  1. ^ Coromines, Joan; Pascual, José Antonio (1983–1991), “medio”, in Diccionario crítico etimológico castellano e hispánico [Critical Castilian and Hispanic etymological dictionary]‎[1] (in Spanish), Madrid: Gredos

Hausa

Indonesian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Indonesian) IPA(key): /ˈmolo/ [ˈmo.lo]
  • Rhymes: -olo
  • Syllabification: mo‧lo

Etymology 1

[edit]

Borrowed from Javanese ꦩꦺꦴꦭꦺꦴ (molo).

Noun

[edit]

molo (plural molo-molo)

  1. (architecture) roof ridge
    Synonym: sirah

Etymology 2

[edit]

Borrowed from Javanese [Term?].

Noun

[edit]

molo (plural molo-molo)

  1. the target in archery

Etymology 3

[edit]

Borrowed from Wolio [Term?].

Verb

[edit]

molo

  1. to dive for pearl shells

Further reading

[edit]
  • “molo”, in Kamus Besar Bahasa Indonesia [Great Dictionary of the Indonesian Language] (in Indonesian), Jakarta: Agency for Language Development and Cultivation – Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology of the Republic of Indonesia, 2016

Italian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈmɔ.lo/
  • Rhymes: -ɔlo
  • Hyphenation: mò‧lo

Etymology 1

[edit]

Of Ligurian origin, from Ancient Greek μῶλος (môlos), μόλος (mólos), itself from Latin mōlēs.

Noun

[edit]

molo m (plural moli)

  1. jetty, pier, mole, quay, dock
Descendants
[edit]
  • → Danish: mole
  • → English: mole
  • → French: môle
  • → German: Mole
  • → Hungarian: móló
  • → Norwegian Nynorsk: molo
  • → Polish: molo
  • → Russian: мол (mol)

Etymology 2

[edit]

See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

Verb

[edit]

molo

  1. first-person singular present indicative of molare

[edit]
  • molo in Treccani.it – Vocabolario Treccani on line, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana

Latin

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Italic *melō (“to grind”), from Proto-Indo-European *melh₂- (“to grind, crush”). Cognate with Latin mollis, Ancient Greek μύλη (múlē), English meal.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [ˈmɔ.ɫoː]
  • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [ˈmɔː.lo]

Verb

[edit]

molō (present infinitive molere, perfect active moluī, supine molitum); third conjugation

  1. to grind or mill
